title: Melba Liston, Dizzy's band and valve trombone players
summary: They mention Melba Liston, Ernie Wilkins and Billy Eckstine, whose valve trombone inspired Maxine.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Now, do you remember Melba Liston (phonetic spelling) the trombone player?
She's back on the scene. Living in Jamaica. The island.
She did the "Salute to Women in Jazz" at the concert we did in June down at the Symphony Space.
She played with a big band, this guy was -- Ernie Wilkins. I saw her playing with Ernie Wilkins, he had a big band at Carnegie Hall.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I think she started with Quincy Jones, then she played with Dizzy Gillespie, didn't she?
Dizzy Gillespie, yes.
She did a lot of arranging --
What do you think of Billy Eckstine's friend strumming the guitar every once in a while.
Well, good for him but he used to play the Valve Trombone.
Valve trombone for Dizzy's band.
That was the inspiration for Maxine picking it up.
That's right.
Now, he's from Pitttsburg.
Yeah, he was born in --
A lot of people think he's from Washington, D.C.
I don't know why.

But Billy's been singing a long time.
Sure.
But he was with Earl Hines -- 'Jelly-Jelly.'
That's right. Sure.
With Walter Fuller on trumpet.
